products.goal: Decide what you will sell and who you will sell it to.
actions: List your initial products or services and identify your target customer.
Choose how customers will purchase: online, in person, subscription or contract.
Check product-specific restrictions before committing to suppliers or inventory.
products.proof: You have a written offer, customer profile and a shortlist of restrictions to verify.

location.goal: Confirm the location can support your intended business before making commitments.
actions: Write down the exact proposed address and intended activities.
Check local permitted use, zoning, lease restrictions and any building approvals.
Contact the relevant city department to confirm uncertainties before signing a lease.
location.proof: You have recorded the location review and any required agency confirmation.

entity.goal: Choose how your business will be legally organized.
actions: Compare the implications of a sole proprietorship, LLC or corporation for your situation.
Check name availability and any naming restrictions with the relevant state authority.
Identify any registered-agent, ownership or filing information required.
Use the state’s official instructions or a qualified adviser before submitting filings.
entity.proof: You have chosen a structure and documented the registration steps and required information.

permit.goal: Find out which registrations, permits or licenses apply to this operation.
actions: Review the legal checklist for your specific industry and business model.
Open the linked government agency sources and verify applicability.
Write down the application, required documents, fee and expected processing time when available.
Apply through the official agency website when ready.
permit.proof: You have identified applicable requirements and recorded submission or approval status.

privacy.goal: Document what information your business collects and how it is used.
actions: List customer, employee and website data you plan to collect.
Determine which privacy and consumer-protection obligations may apply.
Draft policies that accurately reflect your real practices and get appropriate review.
privacy.proof: You have documented your data practices and a plan to review applicable obligations.

contract.goal: Define clear terms for customers, suppliers or clients.
actions: List the parties, scope, pricing, responsibilities and cancellation terms.
Identify intellectual property, refund, liability and dispute questions.
Use qualified legal review where needed before signing or publishing.
contract.proof: You have a reviewed agreement or a list of issues to resolve.

finance.goal: Prepare the registrations and processes needed to handle money.
actions: Check applicable tax registrations and reporting obligations.
Determine what banking, invoicing and recordkeeping setup is needed.
Document due dates and who will maintain the records.
finance.proof: You have a registration checklist and a recordkeeping process.

operations.goal: Prepare to operate safely and reliably.
actions: List operational equipment, people and vendors needed for launch.
Check industry-specific safety, inspection or staffing obligations.
Run a small end-to-end test of ordering, delivery and support.
operations.proof: You have tested the core customer experience and identified unresolved issues.

general.goal: Turn this roadmap item into a concrete deliverable.
actions: Write down the decision or outcome this task requires.
Collect the business information and documents involved.
Review any relevant official requirements or professional guidance.
Save your findings and only mark complete when the outcome is achieved.
general.proof: You can point to a saved decision, document or completed action.

ein_guide.goal: Determine whether you need a federal Employer Identification Number and, if applicable, apply directly through the IRS.
actions: Check IRS guidance on whether your business needs an EIN.
If forming an LLC or corporation, complete state formation first, as directed by the IRS.
Gather responsible party details, legal name, entity type, address and reason for applying.
Use the free IRS EIN application or the appropriate IRS method; save your confirmation notice.
prepare: Legal business name and entity type
Responsible party and taxpayer identification information
ein_guide.proof: You have confirmed whether an EIN is needed and, if applicable, retained the IRS EIN confirmation notice.
